fact: The eFormation application is deployed by the Secrétariat d'Orientation Scolaire, Universitaire et Professionnelle (SOSUP), a state body, according to Focus Groupe Media; the document gives no date for the deployment, so its publication date is used.

The identification operation run through eFormation assigns a unique number to each pupil to follow the school career from pre-primary to the end of studies, in public and private establishments, according to Focus Groupe Media; the document gives no date, so its publication date is used.

SOSUP had for some time been deploying eFormation, giving every establishment and every pupil a unique identifier, while some school promoters and education ministry staff resisted it as intrusive state control, according to Focus Groupe Media; the document gives no date, so its publication date is used.

The document gives no number of establishments or pupils identified in eFormation and no share of schools taking part, and says its success depends on the government overcoming resistance; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

Article 90 of Law 21/2011, signed 14 February 2012, provides that every learner receives from entry to the first pre-primary section a unique coded identification number assigned by the central file of the ministry in charge of National Education, kept until entry into working life; article 94 has the orientation secretariat draw up its list of new baccalaureate holders from that central identification file.

The World Bank's diagnostic says X-Gest, a school management system covering academic events, curriculum, facilities, teachers and students with biometric ID, had been introduced in 92 secondary schools and was expanding to the remaining secondary schools and to primary schools; the passages give no date, so the 2019 publication year is used.

The World Bank's diagnostic says X-Gest lets parents follow through a smartphone app real-time information on school attendance and education scores, in the schools where it has been introduced; the passages give no date, so the 2019 publication year is used.

The World Bank's diagnostic gives 92 secondary schools as having X-Gest and, elsewhere, 106 schools as connected to it out of no stated total, and gives no number of primary schools using it, primary being where it was still to expand; the passages give no date, so the 2019 publication year is used.
